problem_statement:
[Security] NVIDIA API key exposed in process list when creating inference provider
During onboarding, `openshell provider create` is called with the API key interpolated directly into the shell command:

```
openshell provider create --name nvidia-nim --type openai \
  --credential "NVIDIA_API_KEY=${process.env.NVIDIA_API_KEY}" ...
```

While this command is running, any user on the machine can see the full API key via `ps aux`. On shared systems (e.g., DGX Spark), this is a real credential exposure risk.

**Expected:** Pass the credential via stdin, environment variable, or a temporary file with restricted permissions — not as a command-line argument.

Related PRs that partially address this:
- #148 — replace shell string interpolation with argv arrays
- #191 — use provider-specific credential environment variable

problem_statement:
ui.statusLine crashes CLI with spawn EBADF on macOS, then hits ansiRegex3 is not a function
## Summary

Enabling `ui.statusLine` causes Qwen Code CLI to crash after a normal response completes.

The assistant response succeeds, but the status line refresh immediately fails with:

```txt
Error: spawn EBADF
    at ChildProcess.spawn (node:internal/child_process:420:11)
    at spawn (node:child_process:787:9)
    at Object.execFile (node:child_process:349:17)
    at exec (node:child_process:236:25)
    at file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:502641:19
    at Timeout._onTimeout (file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:502672:7)
    at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:585:17)
    at process.processTimers (node:internal/timers:521:7)
```

Then error rendering appears to hit a second issue:

```txt
TypeError: ansiRegex3 is not a function
    at module2.exports (file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:424225:82)
    at stringWidth (file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:424286:17)
    at file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:424335:17
    at Array.map (<anonymous>)
    at ansiAlign (file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:424333:19)
    at makeContentText (file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:511508:40)
    at boxen (file:///opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js:511676:10)
```

## Minimal reproduction

Use this config:

```json
{
  "ui": {
    "statusLine": {
      "type": "command",
      "command": "echo qwen-ok"
    }
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash
qwen -d -i "hello"
```

Observed:

1. Qwen starts normally
2. The prompt is processed normally
3. The assistant returns a normal response
4. Right after response completion, the CLI crashes with `spawn EBADF`

## Notes

This is not specific to a custom shell script.

I reproduced the same crash with both:

```json
"command": "echo qwen-ok"
```

and

```json
"command": "bash ~/.qwen/statusline-command.sh"
```

If I remove `ui.statusLine` entirely, the CLI works normally.

## Relevant code path

The bundled CLI appears to run the status line command here:

- `cli.js:502520`
- `cli.js:502658`
- `cli.js:502679`

It uses `child_process.exec(...)` and then writes JSON to `child.stdin`.

The secondary rendering failure appears around:

- `cli.js:424225`

## Environment

- Qwen Code: `0.14.4`
- Node.js: `v22.22.1`
- OS: macOS Darwin `25.3.0`
- Arch: `arm64`
- Terminal: Ghostty
- `TERM=xterm-ghostty`

## Expected behavior

A failing `statusLine` command should not crash the whole CLI.

At minimum, Qwen Code should ignore the status line failure and continue running.

## Workaround

Removing `ui.statusLine` from config avoids the crash completely.

## Additional observations

- The crash reproduces with a trivial status line command (`echo qwen-ok`), so it does not appear to depend on shell script complexity, `jq`, or Git.
- The main assistant response completes successfully before the crash, so the failure seems to happen specifically during the post-response status line refresh.
- Removing `ui.statusLine` makes the CLI stable again.
- This was reproduced on Node.js `v22.22.1`, so it may be related to Node 22 child process / stdio behavior on macOS.
- The terminal in use was Ghostty (`TERM=xterm-ghostty`), which may also be relevant if the issue depends on TTY handling.

problem_statement:
[ENHANCEMENT] Add Vertex AI support for Claude Opus 4.7 (claude-opus-4-7)
### Problem (one or two sentences)

Vertex users cannot select or use Claude Opus 4.7 (claude-opus-4-7) in Roo Code. 


### Context (who is affected and when)

This affects users with the Vertex provider enabled when choosing models for coding, long-running agent tasks, and high-quality reasoning workloads. The gap appears during model selection and while using Claude 4.x configurations.



### Desired behavior (conceptual, not technical)

Users should be able to choose Claude Opus 4.7 in Vertex just like other supported Claude models. Behavior should feel consistent with existing Vertex Claude support, including optional 1M-context behavior where applicable.

### Constraints / preferences (optional)

_No response_

### Request checklist

- [x] I've searched existing Issues and Discussions for duplicates
- [x] This describes a specific problem with clear context and impact

### Roo Code Task Links (optional)

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria (optional)

Given a user with Vertex as provider

When they open model selection

Then claude-opus-4-7 is available and selectable

And when 1M context is enabled for this model

Then requests use 1M-context behavior consistently with existing Vertex Claude 1M handling


### Proposed approach (optional)

Add claude-opus-4-7 to Vertex model definitions and wire it like existing Opus/Sonnet 4.x entries, then add/update tests for selection and 1M-context behavior.



### Trade-offs / risks (optional)

If provider limits/pricing change after release, metadata may need quick follow-up updates.

problem_statement: Grouped logs breaks alerting ### 🔍 Check for existing issues - [x] Completed ### How is Dozzle deployed? Standalone Deployment ### 📦 Dozzle version v10.3.0 ### ✅ Command used to run Dozzle socket-proxy: image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest container_name: socket-proxy restart: unless-stopped mem_limit: 32m environment: CONTAINERS: 1 INFO: 1 EVENTS: 1 LOGS: 1 STATS: 1 VERSION: 1 POST: 0 AUTH: 0 SECRETS: 0 volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro networks: - socket-proxy-net logging: driver: "json-file" options: max-size: "5m" max-file: "3" dozzle: image: amir20/dozzle:latest container_name: dozzle restart: unless-stopped mem_limit: 64m environment: DOCKER_HOST: tcp://socket-proxy:2375 volumes: - dozzle_data:/data networks: - socket-proxy-net - monitoring-net logging: driver: "json-file" options: max-size: "5m" max-file: "3" ### 🐛 Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it Log alerts are not working properly. The notification channel (Telegram) is correctly configured and functional, as metric and event alerts work perfectly. However, I cannot get log alerts to trigger. While the container filter works as expected, the log filter always returns a validation error: "Ningún registro coincide con este filtro". I have tested several simple filters without success: - message contains "backend" - message contains "info" - message contains "registros" I also tried expressions from the documentation, but the result is the same: - level == "error" - message.status >= 500 - stream == "stderr" Logs from all containers are displayed correctly in the Dozzle UI. I can manually search for the same keywords (backend, info, registros) within the UI, and they return matching records. Example of a log line copied directly from the UI that should match: 2026-04-11T07:46:48.304Z INFO 1 --- [backend] [ main] e.l.backend.services.ElasticSyncService : Sincronizado lote de 1000 registros (Total: 710000) **Edited:** I have two discoveries: first, the contains function is case-sensitive, which is not an issue for my use case. However, the real problem is that if multiple logs occur within the same second, they are ignored by the alerts. Essentially, when logs share the exact same second, the alert fails to trigger as if those logs didn't exist, whereas they work perfectly fine if they are recorded one second apart. problem_statement:
会话锁导致并发消息丢弃：连续发送多条消息只处理第一条
## 问题描述

当用户快速连续发送多条消息（如多张图片）时，cc-connect 只处理第一条，其余消息在会话锁定期间被静默丢弃，session 解锁后也不会补处理。

## 日志证据

```
20:45:17.184 downloaded image  size=244513   ← 第1张，成功下载
20:45:17.184 processing message              ← 第1张，进入处理
20:45:17.195 interactive session started     ← session 被锁
20:45:17.389 message received                ← 第2张消息到达
20:45:17.916 downloaded image  size=266337   ← 第2张，成功下载
20:45:18.003 message received                ← 第3张消息到达
20:45:18.629 downloaded image  size=680155   ← 第3张，成功下载
20:45:47.738 turn complete                   ← 第1张处理完毕
（之后无任何 processing message — 第2、3张被丢弃）
```

## 使用场景

报销场景中员工需要一次性发送多张发票/付款截图。当前只能逐张发送并等待机器人回复后再发下一张，体验很差。

## 期望行为

会话锁定期间收到的消息应该排队等待，session 解锁后依次处理，而不是丢弃。

## 环境

- cc-connect 版本：1.2.1
- 平台：feishu（WebSocket 模式）
- Agent：claudecode

problem_statement:
TypeError: Cannot read property 'on' of null at catchUpgradeRequest
### Expected behavior
Able to proxy websockets with webpack 2.

### Actual behavior
Not able to proxy websockets with webpack 2.

### Setup

webpack-dev-server v2.2.1 was just pushed to stable. It depends on http-proxy-middleware ~0.17.1, which resolves to 0.17.3.

At the previous stable version, v1.16.2, this webpack config works:
```js
  devServer: {
    https: true,
    proxy: {
      '/my-backend': {
        changeOrigin: true,
        pathRewrite: {'^/my-backend': ''},
        target: myBackendUrl,
        ws: true,
      },
  }
```

At v2.2.1, it does not. Instead I get:
```
TypeError: Cannot read property 'on' of null
    at catchUpgradeRequest (/work/my-project/node_modules/http-proxy-middleware/lib/index.js:56:19)
    at middleware (/work/my-project/node_modules/http-proxy-middleware/lib/index.js:48:13)
    at /work/my-project/node_modules/webpack-dev-server/lib/Server.js:223:15
    at Layer.handle [as handle_request] (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/layer.js:95:5)
    at trim_prefix (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:312:13)
    at /work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:280:7
    at Function.process_params (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:330:12)
    at next (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:271:10)
    at middleware (/work/my-project/node_modules/http-proxy-middleware/lib/index.js:43:13)
    at /work/my-project/node_modules/webpack-dev-server/lib/Server.js:223:15
    at Layer.handle [as handle_request] (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/layer.js:95:5)
    at trim_prefix (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:312:13)
    at /work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:280:7
    at Function.process_params (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:330:12)
    at next (/work/my-project/node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:271:10)
    at goNext (/work/my-project/node_modules/webpack-dev-middleware/middleware.js:28:49)
```

problem_statement:
🐞After clicking on YouTube's Dark theme and then YouTube's Light theme, the background doesn't change to Light
## Bug Report:
 - **Description:** In the Themes panel, after clicking on YouTube's Dark theme and then YouTube's Light theme, the background doesn't change to Light. When the previous theme is not YouTube's Dark theme, clicking on YouTube's Light theme changes the background to Light as expected. This bug only occurs when the previous theme is YouTube's Dark theme.
 - **Steps to reproduce this:** Visit YouTube's homepage -> Click on Improvedtube's extension icon -> Click on Themes -> Click on YouTube's Dark (background changes to Dark as expected) -> Click on YouTube's Light (background doesn't change to Light)
 - **Since when?:** I noticed the bug today (March 14, 2026) after I downloaded the extension for the first time.
 - **Browser:** Verified in both Chrome and Firefox
 - **Are any errors shown in the Browser-Console?:**   _(`F12`-key, then `console`-tab)_ No
 - **Does the bug not happen when you log out of YouTube? Then please copy your experiment flags list twice** _(with & without the error to compare). Enter: `yt.config_.EXPERIMENT_FLAGS` into the Browser console on youtube (F12-Key - Or find it in the html source(ctrl+U)_ Bug happens even when I'm not signed in to YouTube


 - Expected preferred behavior: After clicking on YouTube's Light theme, the background should change to Light. But the background doesn't change as expected when the previous background is YouTube's Dark theme.
 - ImprovedTube Version (Written in the Extension header & your Browser's store) 4.2000
 - Tested as only active extension or in incognito mode?: Active
 - OS / Device: Mac

problem_statement: [BUG] SQS: JSON 1.0 requests to /{accountId}/{queueName} are not routed correctly ## Service SQS ## AWS API Action SendMessage, GetQueueAttributes (and other JSON 1.0 SQS operations) ## Expected behavior SQS operations succeed normally — messages are enqueued and attributes are returned. ## Actual behavior Requests are routed to S3Controller instead of the SQS handler, resulting in an XML error response such as: ```xml NoSuchBucketThe specified bucket does not exist Reproduction # Using aws-sdk-sqs gem >= 1.71 (Ruby) or any SDK that sends JSON 1.0 SQS # requests to the queue-URL path rather than POST / > more test.rb require "aws-sdk-sqs" client = Aws::SQS::Client.new( region: "us-east-1", endpoint: "http://localhost:4566", credentials: Aws::Credentials.new("fake", "fake") ) # Create the FIFO queue resp = client.create_queue( queue_name: "test.fifo", attributes: { "FifoQueue" => "true" } ) queue_url = resp.queue_url puts "Created queue: #{queue_url}" # Send a message — this triggers the JSON 1.0 path-routing bug resp = client.send_message( queue_url: queue_url, message_body: "hello from ruby", message_group_id: "group1", message_deduplication_id: "dedup1" ) puts "Sent message: #{resp.message_id}" test.rb (END) gem install aws-sdk-sqs ruby test.rb Environment - Floci version / image tag: hectorvent/floci:latest - How you're running Floci (Docker / native / mvn quarkus:dev): Docker
test_patch:
diff --git a/src/test/java/io/github/hectorvent/floci/services/sqs/SqsJsonProtocolTest.java b/src/test/java/io/github/hectorvent/floci/services/sqs/SqsJsonProtocolTest.java
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..5f82011f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/test/java/io/github/hectorvent/floci/services/sqs/SqsJsonProtocolTest.java
@@ -0,0 +1,166 @@
+package io.github.hectorvent.floci.services.sqs;
+
+import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest;
+import io.restassured.RestAssured;
+import io.restassured.config.EncoderConfig;
+import io.restassured.http.ContentType;
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer;
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Order;
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestMethodOrder;
+
+import static io.restassured.RestAssured.given;
+import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.*;
+
+/**
+ * Integration tests for the SQS JSON 1.0 protocol (application/x-amz-json-1.0).
+ *
+ * Covers two routing modes used by AWS SDKs:
+ * - Root path: POST / with X-Amz-Target header (older SDKs)
+ * - Queue URL path: POST /{accountId}/{queueName} with X-Amz-Target header
+ *   (newer SDKs, e.g. aws-sdk-sqs Ruby gem >= 1.71)
+ */
+@QuarkusTest
+@TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class)
+class SqsJsonProtocolTest {
+
+    private static final String CONTENT_TYPE = "application/x-amz-json-1.0";
+    private static final String ACCOUNT_ID = "000000000000";
+    private static final String QUEUE_NAME = "json-protocol-test-queue";
+
+    private static String queueUrl;
+    private static String receiptHandle;
+
+    @BeforeAll
+    static void configureRestAssured() {
+        RestAssured.config = RestAssured.config().encoderConfig(
+            EncoderConfig.encoderConfig()
+                .encodeContentTypeAs(CONTENT_TYPE, ContentType.TEXT)
+        );
+    }
+
+    // --- Root-path JSON 1.0 (POST /) ---
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(1)
+    void createQueueViaRootPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueName\":\"" + QUEUE_NAME + "\"}";
+
+        queueUrl = given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.CreateQueue")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/")
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200)
+            .body("QueueUrl", containsString(QUEUE_NAME))
+            .extract().jsonPath().getString("QueueUrl");
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(2)
+    void getQueueAttributesViaRootPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueUrl\":\"" + queueUrl + "\",\"AttributeNames\":[\"All\"]}";
+
+        given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.GetQueueAttributes")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/")
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200)
+            .body("Attributes.QueueArn", notNullValue());
+    }
+
+    // --- Queue-URL-path JSON 1.0 (POST /{accountId}/{queueName}) ---
+    // Regression: these requests were previously routed to S3Controller,
+    // returning NoSuchBucket errors.
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(3)
+    void sendMessageViaQueueUrlPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueUrl\":\"" + queueUrl + "\","
+                + "\"MessageBody\":\"hello from json protocol test\"}";
+
+        receiptHandle = null;
+
+        given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.SendMessage")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/" + ACCOUNT_ID + "/" + QUEUE_NAME)
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200)
+            .body("MessageId", notNullValue())
+            .body("MD5OfMessageBody", notNullValue());
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(4)
+    void receiveMessageViaQueueUrlPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueUrl\":\"" + queueUrl + "\",\"MaxNumberOfMessages\":1}";
+
+        receiptHandle = given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.ReceiveMessage")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/" + ACCOUNT_ID + "/" + QUEUE_NAME)
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200)
+            .body("Messages", hasSize(1))
+            .body("Messages[0].Body", equalTo("hello from json protocol test"))
+            .extract().jsonPath().getString("Messages[0].ReceiptHandle");
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(5)
+    void deleteMessageViaQueueUrlPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueUrl\":\"" + queueUrl + "\","
+                + "\"ReceiptHandle\":\"" + receiptHandle + "\"}";
+
+        given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.DeleteMessage")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/" + ACCOUNT_ID + "/" + QUEUE_NAME)
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200);
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(6)
+    void getQueueAttributesViaQueueUrlPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueUrl\":\"" + queueUrl + "\",\"AttributeNames\":[\"All\"]}";
+
+        given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.GetQueueAttributes")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/" + ACCOUNT_ID + "/" + QUEUE_NAME)
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200)
+            .body("Attributes.QueueArn", notNullValue());
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    @Order(7)
+    void deleteQueueViaQueueUrlPath() {
+        String body = "{\"QueueUrl\":\"" + queueUrl + "\"}";
+
+        given()
+            .contentType(CONTENT_TYPE)
+            .header("X-Amz-Target", "AmazonSQS.DeleteQueue")
+            .body(body)
+        .when()
+            .post("/" + ACCOUNT_ID + "/" + QUEUE_NAME)
+        .then()
+            .statusCode(200);
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
fix `FieldOverrider` YAML/JSON log swap and reject empty field overriders
**What happened**:

1. In `applyFieldOverriders` (`pkg/util/overridemanager/overridemanager.go`), YAML patch failures are logged as *"Error applying raw JSON patch"* and JSON patch failures as *"Error applying raw YAML patch"*, the messages are reversed.
2. A `FieldOverrider` can pass validation with only `fieldPath` set and both `yaml` and `json` empty. In that case the code still runs `pointer.Set` with an empty string and **clears the target field** without returning an error.

**What you expected to happen**:

1. Log lines should match the branch (YAML vs JSON) so operators can debug overrides quickly.
2. Either admission should reject a `FieldOverrider` with no YAML and no JSON, or the runtime should return an error instead of silently wiping the field.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**A.  Logs**

- Trigger a failing YAML field override (invalid patch on a string field at `fieldPath`) and check controller logs: the error line says “JSON patch”.
- Trigger a failing JSON field override similarly: the error line says “YAML patch”.

**B.  Silent clear**

- Create an `OverridePolicy` (or `ClusterOverridePolicy`) with `fieldOverrider` containing a valid `fieldPath` pointing at a string field (e.g. a ConfigMap data key) and **omit** both `yaml` and `json` (or use empty arrays).
- Apply the policy to a matching resource and observe propagation: the field at `fieldPath` becomes empty with no admission or apply error.

**Environment**:
- Karmada version:
- kubectl-karmada or karmadactl version (the result of `kubectl-karmada version` or `karmadactl version`):
- Others:
log_parser:
def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import json
    import re

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    def update_status(name: str, status: str) -> None:
        # Fail should always win, then skip, then pass.
        priority = {"fail": 3, "skip": 2, "pass": 1}
        if not name or status not in priority:
            return
        if name in results and priority[results[name]] >= priority[status]:
            return
        results[name] = status

    go_line_re = re.compile(r"---\s+(PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+([^\s]+)")
    pytest_re = re.compile(r"^(.+::\S+)\s+(PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR)\b")
    unittest_re = re.compile(r"^(\S+)\s+\(([^)]+)\)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\b", re.I)
    jest_pass_re = re.compile(r"^\s*[✓]\s+(.*)$")
    jest_fail_re = re.compile(r"^\s*[✕×]\s+(.*)$")
    jest_skip_re = re.compile(r"^\s*[○]\s+(.*)$")

    def parse_output_lines(text: str, pkg: str | None = None) -> None:
        for raw_line in text.splitlines():
            line = raw_line.rstrip()
            if not line:
                continue

            m = go_line_re.search(line)
            if m:
                status = m.group(1).lower()
                test = m.group(2)
                name = f"{pkg}.{test}" if pkg else test
                update_status(name, status)
                continue

            m = pytest_re.match(line)
            if m:
                test = m.group(1).strip()
                status = m.group(2).lower()
                if status == "error":
                    status = "fail"
                update_status(test, status)
                continue

            m = unittest_re.match(line)
            if m:
                test_method = m.group(1).strip()
                test_class = m.group(2).strip()
                status = m.group(3).lower()
                status = {"ok": "pass", "fail": "fail", "error": "fail", "skipped": "skip"}.get(status, status)
                name = f"{test_class}.{test_method}"
                update_status(name, status)
                continue

            m = jest_pass_re.match(line)
            if m:
                update_status(m.group(1).strip(), "pass")
                continue

            m = jest_fail_re.match(line)
            if m:
                update_status(m.group(1).strip(), "fail")
                continue

            m = jest_skip_re.match(line)
            if m:
                update_status(m.group(1).strip(), "skip")
                continue

    for line in log.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        if line.startswith("{") and line.endswith("}"):
            try:
                entry = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                parse_output_lines(line)
                continue

            action = entry.get("Action")
            test = entry.get("Test")
            pkg = entry.get("Package")
            output = entry.get("Output", "")

            if action in {"pass", "fail", "skip"} and test:
                name = f"{pkg}.{test}" if pkg else test
                update_status(name, action)
                continue

            if action == "output" and output:
                parse_output_lines(output, pkg)
            continue

        parse_output_lines(line)

    return results

``` ## Root cause Defuddle preserves tables as content, but tables with zero text across all cells are visual chrome (progress bars, spacers, layout dividers), never data tables. ## Fix direction Strip tables where no cell contains text content.

problem_statement:
Node names should be rfc1123 compliant even when falling back on os.Hostname()
**Describe the bug**
It is possible to have hostnames for machines contain uppercase characters; even if you keep the hostname for the node name it will be lower cased for rfc1123. 

This causes service node label updates to fail as the node does not exist with that name in k8s.

While this configuration is legacy it also seems reasonable to accommodate as this is a known case.

**To Reproduce**
Deploy k8s with upper case host names and use kube-vip with labeling on nodes.

**Expected behavior**
When looking for a node it should give best effort and not intentionally just use a bad value.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS/Distro: [e.g. Ubuntu 1804]
 - Kubernetes Version: [e.g. v.1.18]
 - Kube-vip Version: [e.g. 0.2.3]

**`Kube-vip.yaml`:**
If Possible add in your kube-vip manifest (please remove anything that is confidential)

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

+			name:     "Mixed case hostname is lowercased",
+			hostname: "Worker-Node-1",
+			expected: "worker-node-1",
+		},
+		{
+			name:     "All uppercase hostname is lowercased",
+			hostname: "MASTER-NODE",
+			expected: "master-node",
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			result := normalizeNodeName(tt.hostname)
+			assert.Equal(t, tt.expected, result, "The normalized node name did not match the expected RFC1123 compliant name")
+		})
+	}
+}

problem_statement:
LB listener port for cilium-etcd's etcd cluster not created on GCE
/kind bug

**1. What `kops` version are you running? The command `kops version`, will display
 this information.**

Client version: 1.33.1 (git-v1.33.1)

**2. What Kubernetes version are you running? `kubectl version` will print the
 version if a cluster is running or provide the Kubernetes version specified as
 a `kops` flag.**

**3. What cloud provider are you using?**

GCE

**4. What commands did you run?  What is the simplest way to reproduce this issue?**

kops create cluster cluster.k8s.local \
  --topology private \
  --api-loadbalancer-type internal \
  --networking cilium-etcd \
  --bastion

**5. What happened after the commands executed?**

Cluster built, but cilium pod continually restarted as they couldn't reach APISERVER:4003.  Confirmed that APISERVER isn't configured to listen on port 4003.

**6. What did you expect to happen?**

**7. Please provide your cluster manifest. Execute
  `kops get --name my.example.com -o yaml` to display your cluster manifest.
  You may want to remove your cluster name and other sensitive information.**

```yaml
```

**8. Please run the commands with most verbose logging by adding the `-v 10` flag.
  Paste the logs into this report, or in a gist and provide the gist link here.**

**9. Anything else do we need to know?**

+#!/bin/bash
+set -o errexit
+set -o nounset
+set -o pipefail

+
+

+sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=16777216 || true

+sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_wmem='4096 87380 16777216' || true
+
+
+function ensure-install-dir() {
+  INSTALL_DIR="/opt/kops"
+  # On ContainerOS, we install under /var/lib/toolbox; /opt is ro and noexec
+  if [[ -d /var/lib/toolbox ]]; then
+    INSTALL_DIR="/var/lib/toolbox/kops"
+  fi
+  mkdir -p ${INSTALL_DIR}/bin
+  mkdir -p ${INSTALL_DIR}/conf
+  cd ${INSTALL_DIR}
+}
+
+# Retry a download until we get it. args: name, sha, urls
+download-or-bust() {
+  echo "== Downloading $1 with hash $2 from $3 =="
+  local -r file="$1"
+  local -r hash="$2"
+  local -a urls
+  IFS=, read -r -a urls <<< "$3"
+
+  if [[ -f "${file}" ]]; then
+    if ! validate-hash "${file}" "${hash}"; then
+      rm -f "${file}"
+    else
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  while true; do
+    for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
+      commands=(
+        "curl -f --compressed -Lo ${file} --connect-timeout 20 --retry 6 --retry-delay 10"
+        "wget --compression=auto -O ${file} --connect-timeout=20 --tries=6 --wait=10"
+        "curl -f -Lo ${file} --connect-timeout 20 --retry 6 --retry-delay 10"
+        "wget -O ${file} --connect-timeout=20 --tries=6 --wait=10"
+      )
+      for cmd in "${commands[@]}"; do
+        echo "== Downloading ${url} using ${cmd} =="
+        if ! (${cmd} "${url}"); then
+          echo "== Failed to download ${url} using ${cmd} =="
+          continue
+        fi
+        if ! validate-hash "${file}" "${hash}"; then
+          echo "== Failed to validate hash for ${url} =="

problem_statement:
DNS settings are not propagated when using a base template
### Description

DNS settings are not propagated from base template to main template.
> Discussion on [Slack](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C043N6ZFV9S/p1773853580695349)

## Example:
### Base template:
```yaml
# Debian 13 (trixie) base image
images:
  - location: "https://cdimage.debian.org/images/cloud/trixie/20260316-2418/debian-13-generic-amd64-20260316-2418.qcow2"
    arch: "x86_64"
    digest: "sha512:c6523db54404e320ed30787038f155f649995392697fa2a41e49458d36e056fda020593a03cf910fa7bf93bd5c510b12d6e7c7bf7852a03ee3a64536fecf0127"
  - location: "https://cdimage.debian.org/images/cloud/trixie/20260316-2418/debian-13-generic-arm64-20260316-2418.qcow2"
    arch: "aarch64"
    digest: "sha512:f0460932cd6992539c7c9142bb02a24af83243503bad0179b0813bd6269195785655348ea889daf5927f80853f63b3402a78176967854887dbca9da3859599a0"
  # Fallback images
  - location: "https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/trixie/latest/debian-13-generic-amd64.qcow2"
    arch: "x86_64"
  - location: "https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/trixie/latest/debian-13-generic-arm64.qcow2"
    arch: "aarch64"

mounts: []
# containerd is managed by k3s, not by Lima, so the values are set to false here.
containerd:
  system: false
  user: false
dns:
  - 1.1.1.1
  - 8.8.8.8

hostResolver:
  enabled: false

provision:
  - mode: system
    script: |
      #!/bin/sh
      if [ ! -f /usr/bin/fish ]; then
        apt update
        apt install -y curl gnupg2
        echo 'deb https://download.opensuse.org/repositories/shells:/fish:/release:/4/Debian_13/ /' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/shells:fish:release:4.list
        curl -fsSL https://download.opensuse.org/repositories/shells:fish:release:4/Debian_13/Release.key | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/shells_fish_release_4.gpg > /dev/null
        apt update
        apt install -y fish vim make
        chsh -s $(which fish) {{.User}}
        chsh -s $(which fish)
        hostnamectl set-hostname debian
        reboot
      fi


probes:
  - script: |
      #!/bin/sh
      if ! timeout 30s bash -c "until test -f /usr/bin/fish; do sleep 3; done"; then
           echo >&2 "fish is not installed yet"
           exit 1
      fi

ssh:
  loadDotSSHPubKeys: true

networks:
  - vzNAT: true
    interface: "eth1"

portForwards:
  - ignore: true
    proto: any
    guestIP: 0.0.0.0
vmType: vz
arch: aarch64
cpus: 4
memory: 12GiB
disk: 50GiB
upgradePackages: true
user:
  home: /home/{{.User}}
```
### Main template
```yaml
base:
  - base/debian.yaml
```

### Issue:
DNS setting set on the base template is not propagated to the main template. Not sure if `hostResolver` settings are also propagated.

problem_statement:
Inline nested embeddable generates wrong column name when parent is null
### Describe the bug

When a parent inline embeddable is set to `null`, nested embeddables fail to generate a correct column name.

We were trying to upgrade from 6.4.15 to 6.6.x and our tests started failing.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/atachh/mikro-nested-embeddable-bug

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/sqlite

### MikroORM version

next

### Node.js version

v24.11.0

### Operating system

MacOS

problem_statement:
Custom provider forwards internal namespaced model ID upstream for Fireworks Fire Pass
## Summary
Using Fireworks Fire Pass through a Manifest custom provider appears to send Manifest's internal custom-provider namespaced model ID upstream instead of the raw upstream model name.

Direct calls to Fireworks succeed, but Manifest fails with `NOT_FOUND`.

This seems related to the same general area as #1591, but with a different failure mode: an internal custom-provider routing key appears to leak into the provider request payload.

## Repro
Custom provider config/input:
- Base URL: `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1`
- Model: `accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p5-turbo`

Direct Fireworks request works with those exact values.

However, Manifest logs show the model as:

```text
custom:<provider-id>/accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p5-turbo
```

And the provider response is:

```json
{"error":{"message":"Model not found, inaccessible, and/or not deployed","param":"model","code":"NOT_FOUND","type":"error"}}
```

## Expected behavior
Manifest should send the upstream model unchanged:

```text
accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p5-turbo
```

## Actual behavior
Manifest appears to forward the internal custom-provider namespaced value instead:

```text
custom:<provider-id>/accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p5-turbo
```

## Why this looks like a Manifest bug
- Direct Fireworks curl works with:
  - `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1`
  - `accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p5-turbo`
- So the Fireworks base URL and model ID are valid.
- The failure appears to happen in Manifest's custom provider / model resolution flow.

## Code path suspected
From local inspection of the current code:
- `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts` uses `model: model.id` directly in the OpenAI-compatible request payload
- `src/agents/model-ref-shared.ts` normalizes some built-in providers, but there does not appear to be a custom-provider path that separates:
  - internal routing/model key
  - upstream provider model name

## Important compatibility note
Please avoid fixing this by globally stripping prefixes from all custom-provider model IDs.

That would likely break valid custom providers whose upstream model IDs legitimately contain `/` segments (for example other OpenAI-compatible routers/proxies).

A safer fix would be one of:
1. keep a separate internal routing key vs upstream model name, or
2. strip the prefix only at the exact point where Manifest knows it synthesized the internal `custom:<provider-id>/...` key

## Relation to #1591
This looks related to #1591 in that both involve custom providers and slash-containing model identifiers, but this report is specifically about Manifest leaking an internal namespaced custom-provider model ID into the upstream request payload.

[pickers] Time Picker Changes 12 PM to 11:00 PM When Switching PM to AM on March 8 (DST) ### Steps to reproduce Steps: Live demo: https://stackblitz.com/edit/tjixwd9z?file=src%2FDemo.jsx 1. Open the time picker with the date set to March 8. 2. Set the time to 12:00 PM. 3. Click on the PM field. 4. Type “A” to change PM to AM. 5. Observe the updated time. ### Current behavior - The time changes to 11:00 PM. - The hour is unexpectedly decremented. - This suggests an incorrect hour adjustment during AM/PM toggle, possibly related to DST offset calculations. ### Expected behavior - The time should change from 12:00 PM to 12:00 AM. - Only the meridiem should toggle. - The hour should remain 12. ### Context - Likely issue with 12-hour to 24-hour conversion logic combined with DST adjustment. - This has only been observed on March 8. ### Your environment
npx @mui/envinfo ``` Don't forget to mention which browser you used. Output from `npx @mui/envinfo` goes here. ```

problem_statement:
H2CClient ignores the connect option
## Bug Description

`H2CClient` destructures `connect` from `clientOpts` but does not pass it to `Client`, so the option is ignored.

This appears to be a regression from the refactor where `H2CClient` started extending `Client` directly. As a result:

- custom `connect` functions are not used
- invalid `connect` values are not rejected
- the documented `connect` option for `H2CClient` does not match runtime behavior

## Reproducible By

```js
import { H2CClient } from 'undici'

const client = new H2CClient('http://localhost:3000', {
  connect (opts, callback) {
    console.log('CUSTOM_CONNECT_CALLED')
    callback(new Error('custom connector used'))
  }
})

client.request({ path: '/', method: 'GET' }).catch((err) => {
  console.log(err.message)
}).finally(() => {
  client.close().catch(() => {})
})
```

## Expected Behavior

`CUSTOM_CONNECT_CALLED` should be printed

## Logs & Screenshots

Nothing is printed

## Environment

* macOS 15.1 / Darwin 25.1.0 arm64
* Node.js v24.14.1
* undici 8.0.2

### Additional context

This happens as h2c destructures `connect`, but it's not passed Client
https://github.com/nodejs/undici/blob/743aa8986579dae7f2585c9e17089583787360b3/lib/dispatcher/h2c-client.js#L18-L19

@@ -140,6 +140,32 @@ test('Connect to h2c server over a unix domain socket', { skip: process.platform
   })
 })
 
+test('Should pass custom connect function to Client', async t => {
+  const planner = tspl(t, { plan: 3 })
+
+  const connectError = new Error('custom connect error')
+  const socketPath = '/var/run/test.sock'
+  const client = new H2CClient('http://localhost', {
+    socketPath,
+    connect (opts, cb) {
+      planner.strictEqual(opts.socketPath, socketPath)
+      planner.strictEqual(opts.allowH2, true)
+      cb(connectError, null)
+    }
+  })
+
+  t.after(() => client.close())
+
+  client.request({
+    path: '/',
+    method: 'GET'
+  }, (err) => {
+    planner.strictEqual(err, connectError)
+  })
+
+  await planner.completed
+})

problem_statement:
task --resume-last ignores current-session scoping and can resume another Claude session's task
## Summary

`task-resume-candidate --json` is scoped to the current Claude session, but `task --resume-last` is not. In a multi-session workspace, the CLI can report that there is no resumable task for the current session and then still resume a different session's persisted Codex thread.

The same helper also lets an active task from another Claude session block `--resume-last`, even when `/codex:status` for the current session shows no running jobs.

## Reproduction

1. Start a repository with the plugin state directory available.
2. Run one successful `task` command under Claude session `sess-other` so it persists a completed task thread.
3. In a separate Claude session `sess-current`, run:
   - `node scripts/codex-companion.mjs task-resume-candidate --json`
   - `node scripts/codex-companion.mjs task --resume-last "follow up"`
4. Observe that `task-resume-candidate` reports `available: false`, but `--resume-last` still resumes the older thread from `sess-other`.
5. Alternatively, leave a `running` task owned by `sess-other` in state and run `task --resume-last` from `sess-current`.

## Expected

- Implicit resume selection should use the same current-session visibility rules as `task-resume-candidate`.
- If `CODEX_COMPANION_SESSION_ID` is set and the current session has no resumable task, `task --resume-last` should fail with "No previous Codex task thread was found for this repository.".
- A running task from another session should not block `--resume-last` for the current session.

## Actual

- `task-resume-candidate` says there is no resumable task in the current session.
- `task --resume-last` still resumes another session's completed thread.
- A running task from another session can also block `--resume-last` with `Task ... is still running. Use /codex:status before continuing it.` even though `/codex:status` for the current session shows no running jobs.

## Suspected Cause

`resolveLatestTrackedTaskThread(...)` scans all persisted task jobs in the workspace and only excludes the current job id. It does not apply current-session filtering before choosing a completed thread or before checking for active tasks.

## Suggested Fix

Thread the same session-aware filtering used by `task-resume-candidate` into the implicit `--resume-last` path, and only fall back to `findLatestTaskThread(...)` when there is no Claude session id in scope.

def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    # Regex patterns with named groups: status, name
    patterns = []

    # Symbol-based (Jest-like / node --test with icons)
    # e.g. "✔ test name (4ms)", "✖ test name", "⚠ test name"
    patterns.append(re.compile(
        r'^\s*(?P<mark>[✔✓✖✗⨯❌✕⚠○\-])\s+(?P<name>.+?)(?:\s+\(.*\))?\s*$'
    ))

    # TAP (node --test can output TAP)
    # ok 1 test name
    # not ok 2 test name
    # ok 3 test name # SKIP reason
    patterns.append(re.compile(
        r'^\s*(?P<mark>ok|not ok)\s+\d+\s*(?P<name>.*?)(?:\s+#\s*(?P<directive>SKIP|TODO).*)?\s*$',
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ))

    # Go test
    # --- PASS: TestName (0.00s)
    # --- FAIL: TestName (0.00s)
    # --- SKIP: TestName (0.00s)
    patterns.append(re.compile(
        r'^\s*---\s+(?P<mark>PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(?P<name>.+?)(?:\s+\(.*\))?\s*$'
    ))

    # pytest
    # file.py::test_name PASSED/FAILED/SKIPPED/ERROR
    patterns.append(re.compile(
        r'^\s*(?P<name>[^ ]+::[^ ]+)\s+(?P<mark>PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS)\s*$'
    ))

    # unittest
    # test_method (module.Class) ... ok/FAIL/ERROR/skipped
    patterns.append(re.compile(
        r'^\s*(?P<name>.+?)\s+\.\.\.\s+(?P<mark>ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\s*$',
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ))

    # Generic "PASS/FAIL" prefix line
    # PASS test name
    patterns.append(re.compile(
        r'^\s*(?P<mark>PASS|FAIL|SKIP|SKIPPED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS)\s*[:\-]?\s+(?P<name>.+?)\s*$',
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ))

    # Helper to map status
    def map_status(mark: str, directive: str | None = None) -> str:
        m = mark.lower()
        if directive and directive.upper() in ("SKIP", "TODO"):
            return "skip"
        if m in ("ok", "pass", "passed", "✓", "✔"):
            return "pass"
        if m in ("skip", "skipped", "todo", "xfail"):
            return "skip"
        if m in ("xpass",):
            # treat unexpected pass as pass (could be considered fail, but safer as pass)
            return "pass"
        # anything else is fail
        return "fail"

    for line in log.splitlines():
        line = line.rstrip()
        if not line:
            continue
        matched = False
        for pat in patterns:
            m = pat.match(line)
            if not m:
                continue
            name = (m.group("name") or "").strip()
            if not name:
                continue
            mark = m.group("mark")
            directive = m.groupdict().get("directive")
            status = map_status(mark, directive)
            results[name] = status
            matched = True
            break
        if matched:
            continue

    return results

problem_statement:
Rails layout not applied when using `render :component`
When upgrading from Rails 7.2 to 8, we encountered an issue where controller layouts are no longer applied when using render :component with server-side rendering in react-rails. [This document](https://github.com/reactjs/react-rails/blob/master/docs/controller-actions.md) talks about this use case, specifically "By default, your current layout will be used and the component, rather than a view, will be rendered in place of yield."

In Rails 7.2.2.1 with react-rails 2.6.2, everything works as expected. The problem is introduced in Rails 8 due to a change in the render pipeline: the point at which layouts are applied has shifted. Specifically, the component renderer adds an `inline` key to the render options. In Rails 7.2, the layout was added before this step, so the presence of the inline key didn't affect the layout being applied. In Rails 8, the pipeline was altered so that the component renderer adds the inline key before the layout is applied, which prevents the layout from being included by default.

[This](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/42d75ed3a8b96ee4610601ecde7c40e9d65e003f) is the Rails commit that introduced the change.

def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    def record(name: str, status: str) -> None:
        if name:
            results[name] = status

    # JUnit/XML parsing (best effort)
    if "<testcase" in log:
        stripped_log = log.strip()
        if stripped_log.startswith("<") and ("</testsuite" in log or "</testsuites" in log):
            try:
                import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

                root = ET.fromstring(stripped_log)
                for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
                    name = tc.get("name") or ""
                    classname = tc.get("classname")
                    test_name = f"{classname}.{name}" if classname else name
                    status = "pass"
                    for child in tc:
                        tag = child.tag.lower()
                        if tag in ("failure", "error"):
                            status = "fail"
                            break
                        if tag == "skipped":
                            status = "skip"
                            break
                    record(test_name, status)
            except Exception:
                pass

        def parse_attrs(attr_text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
            return dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"', attr_text))

        for m in re.finditer(r"<testcase\b([^>/]*?)/>", log, re.S):
            attrs = parse_attrs(m.group(1))
            name = attrs.get("name", "")
            classname = attrs.get("classname")
            test_name = f"{classname}.{name}" if classname else name
            record(test_name, "pass")

        for m in re.finditer(r"<testcase\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</testcase>", log, re.S):
            attrs = parse_attrs(m.group(1))
            body = m.group(2)
            name = attrs.get("name", "")
            classname = attrs.get("classname")
            test_name = f"{classname}.{name}" if classname else name
            if re.search(r"<skipped\b", body):
                status = "skip"
            elif re.search(r"<failure\b|<error\b", body):
                status = "fail"
            else:
                status = "pass"
            record(test_name, status)

    # Line-by-line parsing
    minitest_verbose_re = re.compile(r"^(.+?)\s+=\s+[\d.]+\s*s\s+=\s+([.FES])\s*$")
    pytest_re = re.compile(r"^(\S+::\S+)\s+(PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS)\b")
    unittest_re = re.compile(r"^(\S+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|OK|FAIL|ERROR|SKIPPED|skipped)\b")
    go_re = re.compile(r"^---\s+(PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(\S+)")
    jest_pass_re = re.compile(r"^[✓✔]\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\(\d+.*\))?$")
    jest_fail_re = re.compile(r"^[✕✖×]\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\(\d+.*\))?$")
    jest_skip_re = re.compile(r"^[○◌]\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\(\d+.*\))?$")
    tap_re = re.compile(r"^(ok|not ok)\s+\d+\s+-\s+(.+)")

    for line in log.splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue

        m = minitest_verbose_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            name, marker = m.groups()
            status = "pass" if marker == "." else ("skip" if marker == "S" else "fail")
            record(name, status)
            continue

        m = pytest_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            name, status_raw = m.groups()
            status = {
                "PASSED": "pass",
                "FAILED": "fail",
                "ERROR": "fail",
                "SKIPPED": "skip",
                "XFAIL": "skip",
                "XPASS": "fail",
            }.get(status_raw, "fail")
            record(name, status)
            continue

        m = unittest_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            name, status_raw = m.groups()
            status = "pass" if status_raw.lower() == "ok" else ("skip" if "skip" in status_raw.lower() else "fail")
            record(name, status)
            continue

        m = go_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            status_raw, name = m.groups()
            status = "pass" if status_raw == "PASS" else ("skip" if status_raw == "SKIP" else "fail")
            record(name, status)
            continue

        m = jest_pass_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            record(m.group(1), "pass")
            continue

        m = jest_fail_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            record(m.group(1), "fail")
            continue

        m = jest_skip_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            record(m.group(1), "skip")
            continue

        m = tap_re.match(stripped)
        if m:
            ok, name = m.groups()
            record(name, "pass" if ok == "ok" else "fail")
            continue

    return results

def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import json
    import re
    from html import unescape

    results: dict[str, str] = {}
    current_pkg = None

    def normalize_status(s: str) -> str:
        s = s.lower()
        if s in ("pass", "passed", "ok", "success"):
            return "pass"
        if s in ("skip", "skipped", "xfail", "xpass"):
            return "skip"
        return "fail"

    def record(test_name: str, status: str, pkg: str | None = None):
        if not test_name:
            return
        name = f"{pkg}/{test_name}" if pkg else test_name
        results[name] = status

    go_line_re = re.compile(r"^---\s+(PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\(|$)")
    pytest_line_re = re.compile(r"^(.+?::\S+)\s+(PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR)\b")
    unittest_line_re = re.compile(
        r"^(\S+\.\S+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped|SKIP|xfail|XPASS)",
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    jest_re = re.compile(r"^\s*([✓✕○])\s+(.+)$")

    def parse_text_line(line: str):
        nonlocal current_pkg
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        # Update package from go test summary
        m = re.match(r"^(ok|FAIL)\s+\t?(\S+)", line)
        if m:
            current_pkg = m.group(2)
            return

        m = go_line_re.match(line)
        if m:
            status = normalize_status(m.group(1))
            test_name = m.group(2).strip()
            record(test_name, status, current_pkg)
            return

        m = pytest_line_re.match(line)
        if m:
            record(m.group(1), normalize_status(m.group(2)))
            return

        m = unittest_line_re.match(line)
        if m:
            record(m.group(1), normalize_status(m.group(2)))
            return

        m = jest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            sym = m.group(1)
            status = "pass" if sym == "✓" else "fail" if sym == "✕" else "skip"
            record(m.group(2).strip(), status)
            return

    # First pass: line-based parsing (JSON and raw)
    for raw_line in log.splitlines():
        line = raw_line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        obj = None
        if line.startswith("{") and line.endswith("}"):
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                obj = None

        if obj:
            pkg = obj.get("Package") or current_pkg
            if obj.get("Package"):
                current_pkg = obj.get("Package")

            action = obj.get("Action")
            test = obj.get("Test")
            if test and action in ("pass", "fail", "skip"):
                record(test, normalize_status(action), pkg)
                continue

            # Parse output lines for statuses
            if action == "output":
                output = obj.get("Output") or ""
                # Output may contain multiple lines
                for out_line in output.splitlines():
                    out_line = out_line.rstrip("\n")
                    if not out_line:
                        continue
                    m = go_line_re.match(out_line)
                    if m:
                        record(m.group(2).strip(), normalize_status(m.group(1)), pkg)
                        continue
                    # Also parse other frameworks from output
                    m = pytest_line_re.match(out_line)
                    if m:
                        record(m.group(1), normalize_status(m.group(2)))
                        continue
                    m = unittest_line_re.match(out_line)
                    if m:
                        record(m.group(1), normalize_status(m.group(2)))
                        continue
            continue

        # Non-JSON line parsing
        parse_text_line(raw_line)

    # Second pass: parse JUnit-style XML if present
    if "<testcase" in log:
        import re
        try:
            # Remove XML declarations and wrap to ensure a single root
            xml_text = re.sub(r"<\?xml[^>]*\?>", "", log)
            xml_text = f"<root>{xml_text}</root>"
            from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

            root = ET.fromstring(xml_text)
            for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
                name = tc.get("name") or ""
                classname = tc.get("classname") or ""
                full_name = f"{classname}.{name}" if classname else name
                status = "pass"
                for child in tc:
                    tag = child.tag.lower()
                    if tag in ("failure", "error"):
                        status = "fail"
                        break
                    if tag == "skipped":
                        status = "skip"
                        break
                if full_name:
                    results[full_name] = status
        except Exception:
            pass

    return results

problem_statement:
Async Svelte crash in certain situations when destructuring awaited derived value in a @const ### Describe the bug This seems to happen when you have: First, an awaited query, and a derived expression from that query ```typescript import { getIt } from './query.remote.ts'; let d = $derived(await getIt()); // For some reason this additional derived is required to reproduce let showFetchCta = $derived(d.hasData) ``` In the template, a `@const` statement that destructures the awaited value. ```svelte {#if d} {@const {data, hasData} = d} {#if hasData}

The Data: {data}

{:else if showFetchCta}

Fetch now

{:else}

No data

{/if} {/if} ``` Causes the error ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'f') ``` In Module.get where it reads `signal.f` (`signal` is apparently still undefined). If you remove the `@const` destructuring and just reference the values as `d.data` and so on, then it works fine. ### Reproduction https://www.sveltelab.dev/38gut2mu4bw9p4d Note you might have to run with the inspector open to really see the crash. Otherwise it's not totally obvious all the time. ### Logs ```shell Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'f') in in +page.svelte in +layout.svelte in root.svelte in undefined at Module.get (chunk-O3RU4Q5E.js?v=4ba18bce:4157:23) at +page.svelte?t=1774689309840:99:13 at chunk-GMPPHB2E.js?v=4ba18bce:798:5 at update_reaction (chunk-O3RU4Q5E.js?v=4ba18bce:3983:18) at update_effect (chunk-O3RU4Q5E.js?v=4ba18bce:4122:21) at create_effect (chunk-O3RU4Q5E.js?v=4ba18bce:3466:7) at block (chunk-O3RU4Q5E.js?v=4ba18bce:3632:17) at Module.if_block (chunk-GMPPHB2E.js?v=4ba18bce:796:3) at +page.svelte?t=1774689309840:98:16 at Module.add_svelte_meta (chunk-O3RU4Q5E.js?v=4ba18bce:600:12) ``` ### System Info ```shell SvelteLab, also reproduced locally with latest Svelte and SvelteKit ``` ### Severity annoyance

problem_statement:
`.env` file is no longer auto-imported
### Describe the bug

After updating `wxt` from `0.20.20` to `0.20.21`, this error is caused:

> Error: Missing required config: CHROME_EXTENSION_ID, FIREFOX_EXTENSION_ID

I have these environment variables defined in the `.env` file.

This is probably caused by https://github.com/wxt-dev/wxt/pull/2181

```diff
- import { config } from 'dotenv';
```

Simply importing `dotenv/config` auto-imports the `.env` file. From the [README](https://github.com/motdotla/dotenv#readme):

> ```ts
> // index.js
> require('dotenv').config()
> // or import 'dotenv/config' // for esm
> 
> console.log(`Hello ${process.env.HELLO}`)
> ```
> 
> That's it. `process.env` now has the keys and values you defined in your `.env` file.

### Reproduction

- https://github.com/hyunbinseo/better-surf/releases/tag/v0.0.28
- https://github.com/hyunbinseo/better-surf/actions/runs/24392573474/job/71242144892
